title: client_ip still crashes on invalid UTF-8 in X-Forwarded-For — the new decoder's truncation guarantee is bypassed by string.trim
detail: Erlang string:trim raises badarg on invalid UTF-8 (verified: string:trim(<<255,97>>) -> {'EXIT',{{badarg,...}}), so a raw 0xFF byte in the XFF header still 500s the unauthenticated /apply and consent write paths before slice_codepoint_bounded runs. Pre-existing (old code trimmed identically), not a regression, but the fix's documented 'truncation, not a crash' contract holds only for the UA path.
recommended_fix: Move trim/split inside the decoder or make client_ip use byte-safe trimming (e.g. split on byte ',' via binary functions, trim ASCII whitespace) so the codepoint decoder is always reached for arbitrary header bytes.
